name: PopQA
intro: PopQA 是包含 14,267 条问题的开放域事实问答基准。论文从 16 种 Wikidata 关系做流行度加权抽样，每种关系最多 2,000 条，再用人工关系模板、全部可接受宾语与维基百科月度访问量构建问题，用于比较参数记忆、检索增强与自适应检索。
org: University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI, Johns Hopkins University
build_method: Wikidata三元组流行度加权抽样, 每关系最多2,000条, 人工关系模板, 答案闭包, 月度访问量
metric: 精确子串准确率, 各关系准确率, 流行度相关性, 自适应准确率
eval_feature: 16种关系, 流行度加权抽样, 多答案别名, 月度页面访问量, 参数与非参数记忆对比
scale: 14,267条开放域问题, 16种关系, 固定发布17个字段
build_method_en: Popularity-weighted Wikidata triple sampling, 2,000 cap per relation, manual templates, answer closure, monthly page views
eval_feature_en: 16 relations, popularity-weighted sampling, multi-answer aliases, monthly page views, parametric versus non-parametric memory
intro_en: PopQA is an open-domain factual QA benchmark with 14,267 questions across 16 Wikidata relations. The paper uses popularity-weighted sampling capped at 2,000 triples per relation, then manual relation templates, all acceptable objects, and monthly Wikipedia page views to compare parametric memory, retrieval augmentation, and adaptive retrieval.
scale_en: 14,267 open-domain questions, 16 relations, 17 fields in the pinned release
metric_en: Exact-substring Accuracy, Per-relation Accuracy, Popularity Correlation, Adaptive Accuracy

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-22; source_stage=paper-repository-dataset audit; scope=PopQA only. Paper evidence is arXiv:2212.10511v4, submitted as v1 on 2022-12-20 and revised to v4 on 2023-07-02. The fixed PDF URL is https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.10511v4 and its SHA256 is 6de64bcf9b199ae034a09f7e3c407ee6eb0af2bb866335a33445cee95ba1ac38. The paper defines factual knowledge as a subject, relation, object triple and evaluates open-domain QA without a pre-given ground-truth paragraph. PopQA construction randomly samples Wikidata triples from 16 relationship types, but the Appendix makes the sampling non-uniform: a candidate is retained iff f > exp(8R - 6), where R is uniform on (0,1) and f is the exact-match term frequency of the subject entity aliases in an 800 MB random sample of C4. Sampling stops after 2,000 triples for a relation so one relation cannot dominate. The 16 released relations are occupation, place of birth, genre, father, country, producer, director, capital of, screenwriter, composer, color, religion, sport, author, mother, and capital. The paper authors manually write one natural-language template per relation and substitute subject S into the template for R. The acceptable answer set is every entity E for which (S, R, E) exists in Wikidata. Wikipedia monthly page views provide the subject-popularity proxy used in the analysis. Paper Figure 4 reports aggregate n=14,267 and per-relation counts; this graph uses the exact fixed release count rather than rounding it to 14k. Appendix B separately states that 14,282 questions were run through the two GPT-3 models. That 15-question difference is unresolved in the paper and current release. The graph therefore does not assert that the 14,267-row fixed TSV is the same input snapshot used for every reported run. Official repository evidence is https://github.com/AlexTMallen/adaptive-retrieval/tree/8172ab04794a1651488207c230286b0b3786d736 at Git commit 8172ab04794a1651488207c230286b0b3786d736. The downloaded commit tarball SHA256 is f73e5e03d72e313457fb046c9257cda7b6040bcd1e2b03d238dfb1a1180cc44f. The repository has no tagged release. Its data/popQA.tsv SHA256 is 9a5227f41bff0e4c331d4a774d946b12f95307892b58f860a9606ef356e6089b, with 14,267 data rows and 17 columns. The fixed Hugging Face dataset is the author-linked akariasai/PopQA revision 098765c79ea10a2cb19c828324e33281b8336ec0 at https://huggingface.co/datasets/akariasai/PopQA/tree/098765c79ea10a2cb19c828324e33281b8336ec0. Git data/popQA.tsv and HF test.tsv are byte-identical, both SHA256 9a5227f41bff0e4c331d4a774d946b12f95307892b58f860a9606ef356e6089b, and both contain 14,267 data rows. The fixed schema contains id, subject, relation, object, numeric IDs, subject and object aliases, Wikidata URIs, Wikipedia titles, subject and object popularity, question, and possible_answers. This release observation is kept distinct from the paper construction narrative. Evaluation protocol from the paper uses the exact template Q: <question> A:. GPT-Neo and OPT use 15-shot contexts, stratified as one random question-answer example from each of the other 15 relation types; GPT-3 uses zero-shot to control API cost. The official runner supports vanilla, BM25, Contriever, and GenRead. BM25 keeps the full top retrieved passage. The pinned runner's clip_paragraph handles Contriever by splitting the top passage on ". " and joining split[:-1], so it drops the final segment before appending the QA prompt; if no delimiter is present, the result is just ".". GenRead uses the fixed prompt Generate a background document from Wikipedia to answer the given question. {} and then appends the QA prompt. The runner permits 15 new answer tokens, uses temperature 0 and top_p 1 for GPT-3, greedy decoding for local models, removes one leading double newline, and keeps the first output line. Prompt drift is disclosed rather than hidden: the paper says GPT-3 uses zero-shot, the runner default is 15 examples, and the README zero-shot command does not pass --n_examples 0. Therefore executing the documented command literally does not reproduce the paper's GPT-3 shot setting; the diagram directs readers to override the default. A second invocation drift blocks the README Contriever command: README passes --ret_file, while the pinned runner accepts only --ret_path, so the documented command fails during argument parsing unless the flag is corrected. Metric semantics are also separated. The paper marks a prediction correct when any substring of the prediction is an exact match of any gold answer. The pinned runner implements this as pa in pred, pa.lower() in pred, or pa.capitalize() in pred for each possible answer. It does not lowercase the prediction and does not apply punctuation, article, whitespace, token, Unicode, stemming, or general alias normalization beyond the release's possible_answers list and those three gold casings. No LLM judge, human grader, parser model, or adjudication flow is invented. Results use the mean binary accuracy, per-relation accuracy, and correlation between binary correctness and log subject popularity. Adaptive Retrieval is a separate paper analysis over completed parametric and retrieval-augmented predictions: for each relation, 75 percent of PopQA is used to brute-force the popularity threshold maximizing adaptive accuracy, the remaining 25 percent is evaluated, and this is repeated for 100 random splits. Questions below the learned threshold take the retrieval-augmented prediction; the rest take the parametric prediction. The pinned notebook contains this threshold logic but leaves parametric_path and nonparametric_path blank and includes no pinned result files, so it supports algorithm reconstruction, not an independently replayed result claim. The graph keeps paper construction, fixed data release, runner behavior, and adaptive post-processing in separate nodes and dashed boundary cards. All six secondary edges explicitly set style.dashed=true. English and Chinese specs have identical IDs, semantic node types, positions, edges, and modules; English is Chinese-free and Chinese preserves the source distinctions. Fallback Mermaid is generated exactly from the canonical specs. Formal Draw.io, arch, SVG, and PNG assets remain untouched during source stage. Formal publication evidence [site-a12f-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2028×1001 (English) and 2021×1001 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2026×999 and 2019×999. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
